tone.quote: Stress is usually not indicated, since it regularly falls on the penultimate syllable in all Tomini-Tolitoli languages. Only the exceptions to this rule are marked. Primary stress is marked by an acute accent <´>, secondary stress (i.e. lengthening of reduplicated syllables) by a grave accent <`>.

sources.quote: As opposed to 'true' (i.e. etymological) vowels, the paragogic vowel exhibits the following two characteristics: First, it is not relevant in determining the stressed syllable. Stress in Lauje regularly falls on the penultima. Thus, words ending on a paragogic vowel are stressed on the antepenultima. [...] Second, the paragogic vowel never occurs when suffixes are added to a given base form.
sources.locator: printed p. 83, section 1; also abstract, printed p. 81: 'Unlike suffixes, this vowel does not cause a stress shift'
sources.note: Confirms the catalog's fixed penultimate rule for Lauje (catalog cite Himmelmann 1991) and adds a stated exception class: the optional paragogic /e/ (written E) on consonant-final words is invisible to stress, so tutugE 'charcoal', molo'opE 'sufficient' surface with antepenultimate stress (ex. 2, p. 83) while etymological final vowels count (galigo, solipi). Suffixes (-an etc.) do shift stress to keep it penultimate (ex. 3: mongintugE vs meintu-intugan; nosu'ulE vs ponyu'ulan). sources.quote: On Totoli (Lauje's sister language, covered by the same 1991 penultimate-stress statement): 'Totoli shows no evidence of tonal specifications at the level of the word; the language does not make use of word stress nor of lexical tone ... tonal specifications are assigned exclusively at the level of the intonational phrase and are associated with their right-edge boundary.' Also: 'The absence of (post)lexical stress ... may likewise be found in many other languages of the region, as the results from Totoli suggest.' Lauje is never mentioned (0 hits).
sources.locator: Abstract/introduction (front matter p. iv-v and ch. 1, p. 9-10); experimental summary before sec. 3.2
sources.note: Instrumental production+perception study of Lauje's closest documented relative, which Himmelmann 1991 described with the identical penultimate rule; finds no word stress in Totoli. Silent on Lauje, but the natural source for a 'caution' note on the record (Lauje's paragogic-vowel antepenult pattern is itself an argument for word-level stress that Totoli lacks, since Totoli has no paragoge, 1991: 52).
